A lot of ski resorts are being bought up by multinational corporations right now. There's kind of an ongoing war between Vail Resorts and Alterra Mountain Company to accumulate as many different resorts as possible to offer on their competing passes next season. With these deals come very expensive multi-million dollar lift upgrades and replacements. If you think about the cost of shipping all those big lift tower poles, and the fact that they put them in place via helicopter....which in some places takes a very powerful helicopter due to the altitude... It's gotta cost a lot!

The downside is that these deals also generally bring a shit ton more people to these resorts, who can spend a few hundred bucks to visit a dozen or so resorts all year. Realistically the lifts have to be upgraded to get more of them all up the mountain faster. Some of the smaller mountain towns won't even have enough employee housing for the increased support they need, so a lot of the seasonal workers get shelled up in tiny studio apartments with 3 roommates and bunk beds and shit. It's kind of insane.

As with any tourism industry, it's very bittersweet for the locals, because there's always the question of whether more money is worth more crowds and exposure tainting what made these small mountain towns so awesome to begin with.
